title: Clean air conditioner filters
intro: Before summer, clean your split unit's filters: cooler air, fewer smells, lower bills.

steps.t: Switch the unit off with the remote, then unplug it or switch off its breaker.
steps.w: Cut the power, not just the remote: the fan can start while your fingers are inside.

steps.t: Set a sturdy step ladder in front of the indoor unit. No chairs.
Lift the front panel from its bottom edge until it stays open on its own.
Slide out the mesh filters: push them up slightly and pull them down, gently.
Vacuum the dust off the dirty side of the filters, ideally outdoors or over a bin bag.
Wash them in lukewarm water, [[30 °C]] max, with a drop of washing-up liquid. Rinse from the back.
Shake them and leave them to dry in the shade. No sun, no hair dryer: they warp.
steps.label: Drying

steps.t: Meanwhile, wipe the panel and the louvres with a barely damp cloth, unit still off.
Feel the filters: they must be completely dry before you refit them.
steps.fix: If they're damp, wait longer: wet filters grow mould and smell.

steps.t: Slide the filters into their guides the right way round, all the way, and close the panel.
steps.q: Are the filters in their guides and the panel shut?
steps.fix: Pull them out and slide them in along the guides: a crooked filter lets dust straight into the unit.

steps.t: Turn the power back on and run it on cooling for a few minutes: air should flow well, no rattling.

tips: If you use it a lot, clean them every 2 weeks in summer: it cools better and uses less.
Musty smell even with clean filters? The inside coil needs sanitising by a technician.

title: Clean the dishwasher filter
intro: Cloudy dishes or a bad smell? Clean the filter and spray arms to get it washing well again.

steps.t: Switch the dishwasher off. If it has just finished a cycle, let it cool down.
Pull the bottom rack all the way out and set it aside.
Twist the round filter at the bottom anticlockwise and lift it out, then lift out the flat mesh under it.
Rinse the filters under hot water and scrub them with the toothbrush and a drop of washing-up liquid.
Wipe out the well where the filter sits and pick out any bits left at the bottom.
steps.w: There may be glass shards at the bottom: pick them up with gloves or kitchen paper.

steps.t: Take off the lower spray arm: it usually lifts straight up. For the upper one, check the manual.
Clear every hole in the arm with a toothpick, then rinse and shake it until nothing more comes out.
Refit the spray arms until they click and spin them by hand.
steps.q: Do the arms spin freely without touching anything?
steps.fix: If they rub, take them off and refit them until they click. Check nothing in the racks is blocking them.

steps.t: Lay the flat mesh back, insert the round filter and twist it clockwise until it locks.
steps.q: Is the filter locked so it won't lift?
steps.fix: Lift it and twist again until it clicks or the marks line up: a loose filter lets dirt into the pump.

steps.t: Slide the bottom rack back in and run a normal cycle.

tips: Clean it once a month; if dishes come out gritty or smelly, do it now.
Scrape food into the bin before loading: the filter stays clean much longer.

title: Clean the washing machine filter
intro: Not draining or smelly? The pump filter is clogged: clean it in half an hour.

steps.t: Switch the machine off, unplug it and turn off the water tap.
steps.w: Unplug before opening. If you've just run a hot wash, wait: the water can scald.

steps.t: Lay the towels on the floor and slide the shallow tray under the small flap at the bottom.
Open the flap at the bottom front: usually you prise it open with a screwdriver or a coin.
Pull out the small drain hose, remove its cap and let the water run into the tray. Empty it when full.
steps.label: Draining
steps.q: Has the water stopped coming out?
steps.fix: If it's still flowing, empty the tray and wait. No drain hose? Unscrew the filter slowly and let the water out bit by bit.

steps.t: Unscrew the filter anticlockwise slowly, a bit at a time: more water will come out.
Pick lint, coins and hair off the filter and rinse it under the tap until it's clean.
Look into the hole and turn the pump impeller with a finger: it should turn, even if jerkily.
steps.fix: If it's stuck, look for a hairpin or coin jammed in it. If it stays stuck or is broken, call a technician.

steps.t: Refit the filter and screw it clockwise all the way, firmly. Put the hose cap back on.
Plug in, turn the water on and run a short rinse while you watch the flap.
steps.label: Rinse
steps.q: Does the filter stay dry, no drips?
steps.fix: If it drips, unplug, unscrew the filter, check the seal is seated and screw it back in tighter.

tips: Clean it every 3 months, or right away if the machine won't drain or shows a drain error.
Always empty pockets: coins and hairpins are the most common cause of a jammed pump.

title: Defrost a freezer
intro: Thick ice on the walls? Defrost it: it uses less power and the door seals properly again.

steps.t: Move the food into the cool box with ice packs and keep the lid shut.
Unplug the freezer, or the fridge-freezer if it has a single plug.
steps.w: Unplug before you start: you'll be working with water around the appliance.

steps.t: Take out drawers and shelves and lay towels in the bottom and on the floor in front.
Put bowls of hot, not boiling, water inside and close the door. Change the water every 20 minutes.
steps.label: Defrosting

steps.t: Lift out loose chunks of ice by hand or with the plastic spatula, without forcing them.
steps.q: Has the ice come away from all the walls?
steps.fix: If some is left, put in a fresh bowl of hot water and wait another 15 minutes. Never force it.
steps.w: Never use knives or screwdrivers on the ice: you can pierce the refrigerant circuit and ruin the freezer.

steps.t: Wash the inside with warm water and a spoonful of baking soda, then wipe with a clean cloth.
Dry everything thoroughly with a cloth, door seal included.
steps.fix: Wipe again: any water left turns into new ice straight away.

steps.t: Put drawers and shelves back, plug in and set the thermostat as before.
Keep the door shut and wait for it to reach its usual temperature before reloading.
steps.label: Cooling

steps.t: Put the food back quickly and close the door straight away.

tips: Defrost when the ice is over [[5 mm]] thick: the thicker it is, the more power it uses.
Food that has fully thawed shouldn't be refrozen raw: cook it or eat it soon.
A frost-free freezer doesn't need defrosting: just give it a clean now and then.
